To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

unsupervised feature extraction is a promising approach to reading text from natural scenes, and that it can achieve performance that is comparable with the state-of-the-art in the closely related problem of document character recognition.

(i) recognizing digits in natural images is a very difficult computer vision task that requires sophisticated feature representations, (ii) the best existing methods for this task lag well behind human recognition performance and (iii) unsupervised feature learners can achieve state-of-the-art performance on this task.

1) unsupervised feature learners can outperform hand designed features in a real world application, and 2) the best unsupervised feature learner, the convolutional deep belief network (cDBN), is able to learn features that are competitive with the state of the art in the closely related problem of reading digits from handwritten documents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1. Can we reliably recognize digits in natural images? 2. What makes this problem difficult? 3. How do we solve this problem with unsupervised feature extraction?

three main contributions: 1) the introduction of a new, real-world dataset for research use, 2) a detailed analysis of existing methods, and 3) a demonstration of the efficacy of unsupervised feature-learning methods on this problem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we introduce a new dataset for the task of recognizing digits in natural images and show that the task is very difficult for hand crafted features, and that state of the art unsupervised feature learners can solve it with high accuracy.

unsupervised feature discovery methods can outperform hand-designed features for a difficult computer vision application, but that there is still a large gap to the human performance on the very same task.
we have developed a new benchmark dataset, a new algorithm for recognizing digits and a new algorithm for unsupervised feature extraction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance gap between human and machine performance on this task can be significantly narrowed by using unsupervised learning to discover the right features.
unsupervised feature learners are now powerful enough to solve a difficult real world problem that was previously considered to require hand designed features.
unsupervised feature learners are a promising direction of research in this area and are likely to be useful in other computer vision problems.
